Documentation.UserDocu:
viewDefaultOrientation(ori_str = '', scale = -1.0)
Sets camera rotation to a predefined one, and camera position and zoom to show certain amount of model space.
ori_str: orientation, can be 'Top', 'Bottom', 'Front', 'Rear', 'Left', 'Right', 'Isometric', 'Dimetric', 'Trimetric', 'Custom'. If empty, the value is fetched from Parameters. scale: sets distance from camera to origin, and height of the screen in model space, so that a sphere of diameter 'scale' fits the height of the viewport. If zero, scaling is not done. If negative, the value is fetched from Parameters.

saveImage(path, width=-1, height=-1, background='Current', comment='$MIBA', samples=..., wait=True)
Write the view to an image file. A width or height of -1 keeps the view's own. 'background' is a color name, or 'Current' for the view's. wait=True (the default) captures a COMPLETE backend frame, with every user shader compiled and every deferred shape arrived (waitFrameComplete); wait=False takes the next frame as it stands.
With an external render backend active (render cache mode 3) the scene is drawn by the backend, not by the Coin scene graph, so the capture is taken through the backend's own frame readback instead (docs/RenderDebug.md section 4). The image is of the model: the navigation cube, the corner axis cross and on-screen text are left out of it, while in-scene overlays (editing overlays, dimensions) stay. Two limits come with the readback -- it is taken at the view's resolution and scaled if another size is asked for, and its background is opaque. saveRenderDump(source='renderer') captures the same frame as staged, chrome included, when that is what you want.

cyclesRender(path, width=640, height=480, samples=64, device='CPU', wait=True) -> dict
Path trace this view with the Cycles engine to a PNG at path (docs/CyclesIntegration.md phase 3): the view's render-cache scene, its PBR/output/light/background settings and its current camera, framed for width x height, with samples per pixel on the named device ("CPU", "CUDA", ...). Blocks until the render is done. With wait=True (the default) it waits first for a complete frame (waitFrameComplete), so the scene it traces is whole: a publish still catching up deferred shapes would otherwise trace half of it; wait=False traces the scene as it stands. Requires the render-cache bridge (render cache mode 3) and a build with BUILD_CYCLES.
Returns a dict of what the translation made of the scene: meshes, objects, shaders, triangles, skipped (draws with no path-traced form: lines, points, gizmos, effect volumes), seconds.

cyclesViewport(enable=True, device='CPU', samples=256, timeLimit=0.0, denoise=True, pixelSize=1)
Path trace this view live with the Cycles engine (docs/CyclesIntegration.md phase 4): a session on the named device ("CPU", "CUDA", ...) follows the view's scene, settings and camera, and its progressively refined frame is drawn as the base layer of every frame, under the selection highlight. samples is the budget per pixel before the render rests, timeLimit a cap in seconds (0 = none), denoise applies OpenImageDenoise (fast quality) as the frame refines, pixelSize renders at 1/n resolution and scales up (Blender's preview pixel size). enable=False turns it off. Requires the render-cache bridge (render cache mode 3), a render backend and a build with BUILD_CYCLES.

cyclesViewportStatus() -> dict or None
What the live Cycles session of this view is doing, or None when cyclesViewport() is off: running, progress (0..1), complete (the session has rendered its whole sample budget for the scene and camera as last stated, with no error -- the built-in signal a test polls instead of sleeping), status (the engine's text), error, the translation report of the scene as last stated (meshes, objects, shaders, triangles, skipped), what the last translation did (added, removed, restated objects; built, released meshes), and how the scene got there: sessions (started, each a device set-up) and updates (scenes restated in place under a running session).

waitFrameComplete(timeout=120000) -> bool
Run frames until the external render backend has rendered a COMPLETE one since the call (docs/RenderDebug.md section 4.2): every user shader compiled, every shape the publish deferred under its capture budget arrived, a frozen frame's particle warm-up reached, no mesh refine outstanding -- the picture, rather than a number of frames. The built-in signal a test settles on before it captures or measures; saveRenderDump and cyclesRender wait for the same thing themselves. The quiet timeout (5 s) restarts on every frame rendered and every pending compile; timeout (ms) bounds the whole wait. Without a backend one frame is rendered. False on timeout.

isFrameComplete() -> bool
Whether the last frame the external render backend rendered was complete (see waitFrameComplete). True without a backend.

saveRenderDump(path, source='renderer', mode=None, metadata=True, wait=True)
One-shot render frame capture with reproducibility metadata (docs/RenderDebug.md section 4). Returns the written image path (source='viewer': list of paths, one per connected viewer).
wait=True (the default): the capture is of a COMPLETE frame -- every user shader compiled, every shape the publish deferred arrived, the frozen particle warm-up reached (waitFrameComplete). wait=False takes the very next frame as it stands, mid-arrival included, which is what a probe of the arrival itself wants. Not applicable to source='viewer' (the browser reads back its own canvas).
source='renderer': readback of the external render backend's scene color target (the true desktop-GPU frame, before the Coin composite). source='framebuffer': the composited frame (saveImage path). source='viewer': push a dumpFrame request to every WASM viewer connected to the scene-streaming server; each viewer reads back its canvas on its own GPU and uploads the pixels.
mode: temporary RenderDebug_ViewMode for the captured frame only (renderer/viewer sources). metadata: write a '<path>.json' sidecar (camera, viewport, backend, active Render_*/RenderDebug_* values) so the frame can be re-staged.

getRenderStats(wait=True)
Capture one frame of the external render backend and return its readback statistics as a dict: width, height, geometryPixels (pixels covered by geometry, i.e. depth in front of the far plane) and avgColor of those pixels — the cheap numeric assertions for render smoke tests (docs/RenderDebug.md section 4.2). wait=True (the default) reads a COMPLETE frame (see waitFrameComplete); wait=False reads the very next one as it stands.
The dict also carries the backend's handle-pool occupancy, each beside its limit: frameBuffers/maxFrameBuffers, textures/maxTextures, views/maxViews, plus textureMemory, renderTargetMemory, gpuMemoryUsed and gpuMemoryMax in bytes (-1 where the backend does not report one). These are PROCESS-WIDE -- every open 3D view and the scene server draw from the same pools -- so they answer "how many more views fit", which is not a question any single view can answer about itself.

reloadShaders()
Reload the external render backend's shader programs from disk on the next rendered frame (docs/RenderDebug.md section 3). With FC_BGFX_SHADER_DIR pointing at a development asset tree, recompiling a shader (src/Gui/Renderer/bgfx/shaders/compile.sh) followed by this call is a live edit-save-see loop — no restart.

getViewDirection()
Returns the direction vector the view is currently pointing at as tuple with xyz values

setViewDirection()
Sets the direction the view is pointing at. The direction must be given as tuple with three coordinates xyz

getCursorPos() -> tuple of integers
Return the current cursor position relative to the coordinate system of the viewport region.

getObjectInfo(tuple(int,int), [pick_radius]) -> dictionary or None
Return a dictionary with the name of document, object and component. The dictionary also contains the coordinates of the appropriate 3d point of the underlying geometry in the scenegraph.
If no geometry was found 'None' is returned, instead.

getObjectsInfo(tuple(int,int), [pick_radius]) -> dictionary or None
Does the same as getObjectInfo() but returns a list of dictionaries or None.

getPointOnViewport(3D vector) -> pixel coords (as integer)
Return the projected 3D point (in pixel coordinates).

getPointOnFocalPlane(pixel coords (as integer)) -> 3D vector
Return the according 3D point on the focal plane to the given 2D point (in pixel coordinates).

getPoint(pixel coords (as integer)) -> 3D vector
Return the according 3D point on the focal plane to the given 2D point (in pixel coordinates).

addDraggerCallback(SoDragger, String CallbackType, function)
Add a DraggerCalback function to the coin node Possibles types : 'addFinishCallback','addStartCallback','addMotionCallback','addValueChangedCallback'

removeDraggerCallback(SoDragger, String CallbackType, function)
Remove the DraggerCalback function from the coin node Possibles types : 'addFinishCallback','addStartCallback','addMotionCallback','addValueChangedCallback'

getViewProvidersOfType()
Returns a list of view providers for the given type
redraw(): reders the scene on screen (useful for animations)

setName(str): sets a name to this viewer
The name sets the widget's windowTitle and appears on the viewer tab
getName() -> string: return the window Title of this view

toggleClippingPlane(toggle=-1, beforeEditing=False, noManip=True, pla=App.Placement() Toggle a global clipping plane
toggle: -1 toggle, 1 show, 0 hide beforeEditing: whether to insert the clipping node before or after editing root node noManip: whether to create a manipulator pla: clipping plane placement
hasClippingPlane(): check whether clipping plane is active

addObjectOnTop(obj,subname='')
Force showing an object in group on top

removeObjectOnTop(obj,subname='')
Remove an object (or all objects if none is given) from on top group

isObjectOnTop(obj,subname='')
Check if a given object is in group on top

getObjectsOnTop(alt=True : Boolean) -> List[Tuple[DocumentObject, String]]
Return the list of objects on top

bindCamera(node, sync=False)
Bind a camera node to the camera of this view. node: camera Coin3D node. Pass 'None' to unbind. sync: determines whether to sync the camera setting up on binding.

bindView(view|view_title)
Bind the camera of the given view to the camera of this view.

unbindView(view|view_title|None)
Unbind the camera of the given view to the camera of this view. Pass 'None' to unbind all views. To function works bi-directionally.

boundView() -> view
Return the bound view. Note that view camera binding is bi-directional. But this function only returns the view bound by calling bindView(). To obtain all bound views, use boundViews()

boundViews(recursive=False) -> List[view]
Return all views that are bound to this view.
graphicsView(): Access this view as QGraphicsView
setCornerCrossVisible(bool): Defines corner axis cross visibility
isCornerCrossVisible(): Returns current corner axis cross visibility
setCornerCrossSize(int): Defines corner axis cross size
getCornerCrossSize(): Returns current corner axis cross size
